sites_https_justification: All project sites are served over HTTPS: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pslr , https://bart-turczynski.gitlab.io/pslr/ , and https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=pslr .
description_good_justification: DESCRIPTION and README provide a clear, succinct description of what pslr does: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pslr#readme
interact_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md explains how to interact with and contribute to the project: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pslr/-/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states the requirements for acceptable contributions: Air formatting and a clean run of fleet-ci's local gate (`.fleet-ci/gate`, lint, docs drift, spelling, README drift, the URL check and R CMD check --as-cran in a container), the pre-push gate rather than hosted CI: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pslr/-/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md . The coding, testing and documentation rules it builds on, including that new code requires tests, are in https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pslr/-/blob/main/docs/r-conventions.md
license_location_justification: LICENSE is at the repository top level: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pslr/-/blob/main/LICENSE
floss_license_osi_justification: MIT is an OSI-approved open source license: https://opensource.org/license/mit
documentation_basics_justification: Basic documentation in the README and the pkgdown site, plus package vignettes: https://bart-turczynski.gitlab.io/pslr/
documentation_interface_justification: Every exported function is documented (roxygen2 man pages) and published on the pkgdown reference index: https://bart-turczynski.gitlab.io/pslr/reference/index.html
repo_track_justification: All changes are tracked in git: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pslr/-/commits/main
repo_interim_justification: Interim development commits are publicly available on GitLab between releases: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pslr/-/commits/main
repo_distributed_justification: Uses git, a distributed version control system: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pslr
version_unique_justification: Each release carries a unique version (DESCRIPTION Version; CRAN enforces uniqueness): https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=pslr
version_semver_justification: Uses semantic-style x.y.z versioning; the published releases are tagged v1.0.0 through v1.2.1 at https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pslr/-/tags
version_tags_justification: Every release is tagged in git as v<version> and the tags are published in the public repository: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pslr/-/tags
release_notes_justification: NEWS.md documents user-facing changes for each release: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pslr/-/blob/main/NEWS.md
release_notes_vulns_justification: No publicly known vulnerabilities have been fixed to date; NEWS.md records all changes: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pslr/-/blob/main/NEWS.md
report_tracker_justification: GitLab work items serve as the public issue tracker: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pslr/-/work_items
report_process_justification: Users submit bug reports through the GitLab issue tracker: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pslr/-/work_items. DESCRIPTION's BugReports: field names the same address.
report_responses_justification: Maintainer responds to issue reports on the tracker: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pslr/-/work_items
enhancement_responses_justification: Maintainer responds to enhancement requests on the tracker: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pslr/-/work_items
report_archive_justification: GitLab work items provide a publicly available, searchable archive of reports and responses, open and closed: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pslr/-/work_items
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: The vulnerability-reporting process is published in the security policy: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pslr/-/blob/main/SECURITY.md . Reports go to the maintainer by email at bartek@turczynski.pl with 'pslr security' in the subject; the policy states explicitly that vulnerabilities must not be filed on any public issue tracker.
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: Private reporting is by direct email to the maintainer (bartek@turczynski.pl), documented as the sole confidential channel in SECURITY.md: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pslr/-/blob/main/SECURITY.md . The project deliberately does not rely on a forge-hosted advisory workflow, so the channel does not depend on the maintainer's account status at any single forge.
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: SECURITY.md commits to acknowledging reports within 7 days and coordinating a fix and disclosure: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pslr/-/blob/main/SECURITY.md
build_justification: Builds with the standard R toolchain (R CMD build / INSTALL, devtools) plus cpp11 for the C++ PSL matcher: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pslr
build_common_tools_justification: Uses the standard, widely available R build tooling with GCC/Clang via cpp11.
build_floss_tools_justification: R, GCC/Clang, and the entire build toolchain are free/open source software: https://www.r-project.org/
test_invocation_justification: Tests run via devtools::test() and as part of R CMD check.
test_most_justification: Coverage is measured with covr in the `coverage` job (fleet-ci's template, included by .gitlab-ci.yml), which fails below 95% and publishes a Cobertura report and a coverage percentage (95.27% on the last CRAN-prep pipeline, 2026-08-09). It runs on the weekly T2 deep-check pipeline schedule and on every RELEASE=1 pre-submission pipeline: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pslr/-/blob/main/.gitlab-ci.yml
test_policy_justification: The project's coding conventions require tests for new code, and for each new user-facing function: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pslr/-/blob/main/docs/r-conventions.md
tests_are_added_justification: New functionality ships with tests, as docs/r-conventions.md requires (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pslr/-/blob/main/docs/r-conventions.md); `R/foo.R` is tested by `tests/testthat/test-foo.R`: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pslr/-/tree/main/tests/testthat
tests_documented_added_justification: The test-addition policy ("New code requires tests.") is documented in docs/r-conventions.md, reached from CONTRIBUTING.md through docs/git-workflow.md and named in AGENTS.md: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pslr/-/blob/main/docs/r-conventions.md
warnings_justification: Warnings are surfaced by lintr and by R CMD check. Both run in the local pre-push gate (T1, fleet-ci's `.fleet-ci/gate` in a container) before every push that is not docs-only, once the clone has the hook installed (`.fleet-ci/pre-push --install`), and R CMD check again in the CI check jobs on the weekly T2 deep-check schedule and every RELEASE=1 pipeline: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pslr/-/blob/main/.fleet-ci.yml
warnings_fixed_justification: Warnings are treated as errors and fixed; R CMD check is kept clean.
warnings_strict_justification: Any lint fails the build: the local pre-push gate (T1) runs `lintr::lint_package()` and fails if it returns anything, and runs R CMD check --as-cran with error_on = "warning" — a warning is a build failure, not a report. The T2 check jobs fail on any ERROR or WARNING: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pslr/-/blob/main/.fleet-ci.yml
know_secure_design_justification: The maintainer applies secure design principles; pslr defensively handles untrusted host strings through its C++ PSL matcher, enforcing strict input parsing and trie-based label matching.
know_common_errors_justification: The maintainer is aware of common C++ memory-safety pitfalls (buffer overflows, integer overflows) and PSL-matching edge cases (wildcards, exception rules). The C++ matcher core is covered by clang-ASAN/UBSAN and valgrind in dynamic analysis.
crypto_password_storage_justification: pslr stores no passwords or credentials.
crypto_random_justification: pslr does not generate security-sensitive random values.
crypto_used_network_justification: pslr's only network access is psl_refresh(), which runs only when the user calls it. It accepts only https URLs, rejecting any other scheme, embedded credentials, a query string or a fragment, and it follows redirects itself one hop at a time, refusing any hop that leaves https or the original origin: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pslr/-/blob/main/R/url-policy.R
crypto_tls12_justification: psl_refresh() makes its https requests through the curl R package, that is, through libcurl and its TLS backend, which support TLS 1.2 and later. pslr never sets or lowers the TLS version, so the version negotiated and the minimum accepted are libcurl's and the backend's, not pslr's: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pslr/-/blob/main/R/http-transport.R
crypto_certificate_verification_justific: psl_refresh() leaves libcurl's certificate and host-name verification at its defaults, which are on: pslr never sets ssl_verifypeer or ssl_verifyhost, and a certificate that fails verification aborts the refresh with a transport error. The check is libcurl's default, which pslr does not override, rather than code of pslr's own: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pslr/-/blob/main/R/http-transport.R
crypto_verification_private_justificatio: pslr sends no cookies or credentials, and it rejects a URL that embeds them. The only request headers it adds are User-Agent, Accept-Encoding and the cache validators (If-None-Match or If-Modified-Since), and a validator goes only to the exact URL that issued it. Every request is https, so libcurl completes certificate verification in the TLS handshake before any HTTP header is sent: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pslr/-/blob/main/R/url-policy.R
delivery_mitm_justification: Distributed via CRAN and GitLab over HTTPS; CRAN publishes per-package checksums: https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=pslr
delivery_unsigned_justification: All distribution downloads are served over HTTPS (CRAN, GitLab, r-universe); no hash is retrieved over plain HTTP: https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=pslr
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: No outstanding known vulnerabilities; tracker at https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pslr/-/work_items
static_analysis_justification: lintr (full-package lint, its linter set kept in step with goodpractice's via .lintr) and R CMD check --as-cran run in the local pre-push gate (T1) before every push that is not docs-only, once the clone has the hook installed (`.fleet-ci/pre-push --install`), and R CMD check again in the CI check jobs on the weekly T2 deep-check schedule and every RELEASE=1 pipeline: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pslr/-/blob/main/.fleet-ci.yml
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: lintr and R CMD check --as-cran (including C++ compiler warnings from the PSL matcher) find defects but are not vulnerability scanners, and no vulnerability-focused analyzer such as cppcheck, clang-tidy or flawfinder runs over src/. The osv-audit and security-audit jobs check dependencies against OSV and OSS Index weekly and before each release, but that is SCA, not static analysis of pslr's code: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pslr/-/blob/main/.gitlab-ci.yml
static_analysis_fixed_justification: Static-analysis findings are addressed before merge.
static_analysis_often_justification: lintr runs on every push that is not docs-only, as a gate of the local pre-push gate (T1), and fails the push on any lint. That hook is local, so a reviewer cannot inspect or verify it, and it is bypassed by `git push --no-verify` or by a clone that never ran `.fleet-ci/pre-push --install`; no hosted job runs lintr: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pslr/-/blob/main/.fleet-ci.yml
dynamic_analysis_justification: The C++ PSL matcher runs under ASAN/UBSAN in two CI jobs on the weekly T2 deep-check schedule and on every RELEASE=1 pre-submission pipeline: `x-sanitizers-gcc` (the testthat suite over a gcc -fsanitize=address,undefined build) and `t2-sanitizers` (R CMD check, test suite included, in R-hub's clang-asan container): https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pslr/-/blob/main/.gitlab-ci.yml . Before releases, `tools/verify.sh sanitize` also runs the suite under ASAN/UBSAN and valgrind in Docker: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pslr/-/blob/main/tools/verify.sh
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: pslr ships C++ code in src/ (the PSL matcher: cpp11.cpp, matcher.cpp). ASAN/UBSAN (memory errors and undefined behavior) run over it weekly and before each release in the `x-sanitizers-gcc` and `t2-sanitizers` CI jobs, and `tools/verify.sh sanitize` adds valgrind (memory leaks and illegal memory access) before releases: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pslr/-/blob/main/.gitlab-ci.yml
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: pslr's automated test suite uses testthat, whose expectations (expect_*) are assertions checked at runtime; the suite runs in R CMD check in the local pre-push gate (T1) before every code push: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pslr/-/tree/main/tests/testthat . The `x-sanitizers-gcc` and `t2-sanitizers` CI jobs additionally run it under ASAN/UBSAN, enabling runtime memory and undefined-behavior assertions over the C++ PSL matcher, weekly and before each release, and `tools/verify.sh sanitize` under valgrind before releases: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pslr/-/blob/main/.gitlab-ci.yml
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: Any issues surfaced by the sanitizer or valgrind runs are fixed before release.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: Stated as unmet rather than described around. No pipeline runs on integration events: fleet-ci's template, which .gitlab-ci.yml includes, creates no pipeline for a push to main, a branch push or a merge request. The per-change gate is fleet-ci's local gate (T1: lint, docs drift, README drift, the URL check, R CMD check --as-cran and the locale assertion, in a container), run by a local pre-push hook, which a reviewer cannot inspect and which `git push --no-verify` bypasses. A weekly T2 deep-check schedule and every RELEASE=1 pre-submission pipeline, on the maintainer's self-hosted GitLab runner, give an independent clean-checkout run of main (R CMD check on R release, oldrel, devel and the declared floor, --as-cran with incoming checks, two sanitizer legs, the locale legs, coverage and the dependency audits): https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pslr/-/blob/main/.gitlab-ci.yml
discussion_justification: Discussion happens on GitLab work items and merge requests, which are public, searchable and addressable by URL, and need no proprietary client software: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pslr/-/work_items
no_leaked_credentials_justification: No credentials are committed. A gitleaks scan of the full git history (306 commits across all refs, 2026-09-26) found no leaks: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pslr
english_justification: Documentation and issue-tracker interaction are conducted in English (Language: en-US): https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pslr#readme
hardening_justification: pslr applies no hardening of its own. Its C++ matcher is compiled with the flags of the user's R installation (the package has no src/Makevars), so stack protection or _FORTIFY_SOURCE apply only where that R build or the platform turns them on, and CRAN policy discourages a package from setting non-portable compiler flags itself. The sanitizer CI jobs and the sanitize tier of tools/verify.sh (ASAN/UBSAN and valgrind) find memory defects before a release, but they are testing, not a hardening mechanism in the software shipped.
sites_password_security_justification: Project sites (GitLab, CRAN) manage their own authentication; pslr operates no site with user passwords.
maintained_justification: Actively maintained: recent CRAN releases, frequent commits, and responsive issue handling: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pslr/-/commits/main
